BIT SHIFT, FIFO & LIFO INSTRUCTIONS
In this lesson, we will look at the bit shift, FIFO, and LIFO instructions. As you will see, these instructions have many operational similarities.

DISCUSSION
Bit shift instructions, as the name implies, are used to shift bit values in one of two directions. The FIFO and LIFO instructions are used to shift words.
The table below shows all of the instructions that we will examine in this lesson. Each of the three instruction types include two instructions, which gives us a total of six instructions...
2. Use The Programming Device 4. Consult Flow Charts
Let's start by examining the bit shift instructions. Before looking at the actual instructions, it is important to understand what functionality a bit shift instruction provides.

Bit shifting allows you to shift bits in words either left or right. This means that a new bit will be placed on one side and one bit will be effectively pushed out the other side. The sides depend on which direction bit shift you use......

One application for bit shifts is to send a certain sequence of bits into a single bit that corresponds to an output. This way, you can have a pattern for that output to follow based on each bit as it's shifted into the particular bit position...

In the example below, you can see how the output of the light corresponds to the bits that are shifted into the word containing that output. Notice the other bits are affected in the output word since their values are also being shifted.......................

In our example, we have shifted in zeros, but this is not always the case. You can shift other data into the data file you are modifying. This will become clear as you learn about the actual instructions used by the PLC...

This is the Bit Shift Left (BSL) instruction. This instruction requires four parameters: a file, control, bit address, and length. The file is the data file which contains the bits that you want to shift...
CONTROL FILE

The control is a data file used by the instruction to keep track of the current status and result of the Bit Shift Left instruction. This data element contains three words which contain various status bits...
0 EN DN ER UL NOT USED
1 SIZE OF BIT ARRAYY ER UL NOT USED
2 BIT POINTER
EN - ENABLE DN - DONE
ER - ERASE UL - UNLOAD
The enable bit indicates that the logic preceding this function had a true path and a bit shift is going to be performed. The done bit indicates that a shift has been successfully made.
The error bit indicates an error has occurred because of the parameters set in the instruction. Normally, this means that a negative value was entered for the length parameter, which is not valid...

The unload bit contains the bit that was shifted out of the file once the instruction was evaluated. This bit can be accessed with the bit functions to determine results or conditions of the instruction. No other instruction should modify this control file...

The next parameter is the bit address, which points to the location of a bit in memory that will be shifted into the right side of the file data. As the parameter implies, you must specify an address...

The last parameter is the length. The length specifies how many bits are being used in the file data. It is important for the instruction to know what the last bit is, so it can be shifted out and into the unload bit of the control file...

It is important to note if the length you specify only uses part of the last word that some of the bits are in, all other unused bits will be ignored by the instruction. The importance of remembering this cannot be stressed enough...
The maximum allowable size is 2048 bits. Be careful, however, that you do not specify too many bits. Exceeding 2048 bits will cause an error.
Here is an example of the instruction. Notice that following the false to true logic condition in the rung, the bit shift left occurs and the last value is placed into the control file.
The Bit Shift Right (BSR) instruction requires the same parameters as the Bit Shift Left instruction. The difference
is that all bits are shifted right instead of left.
CONTROL FILE
0 EN DN ER UL NOT USED
1 SIZE OF BIT ARRAYY ER UL NOT USED
2 BIT POINTER
EN - ENABLE DN - DONE
ER - ERASE UL - UNLOAD
For this reason, the rightmost bit is loaded into the unload bit of the control file and the new bit (pointed to by the bit address) is loaded into the left side.

A neat little trick is wrapping around the bits so it shifts the last bit into the first bit location. To do this, you place the bit address to be unload bit. This is useful when you want to shift the same values in a continuous loop...
How many parameters do the BSL and BSR instructions require?
Remember, these instructions require four parameters: a file, control, bit address, and length.
TRY AGAIN!
The next instructions that we will examine are the FIFO (First In, First Out) instructions. These instructions involve storage of data in memory. The method of storage is comparable to a queue...
2. Use The Programming Device 4. Consult Flow Charts

There are two instructions used for this operation. The name "First In, First Out" refers to how words are entered and removed from the stack. A stack, as its name implies, is a stack of data words in memory that is used to store temporary data, like a scratch pad...

This is the FIFO Load (FFL) instruction, which is used to take a word value and place it into the stack for your later use. The five parameters required by the FIFO Load instruction are shown below...
The source is the word location or actual value that you want to place onto the stack. The FIFO is the stack data file in memory. You can have multiple stacks depending on their size.
CONTROL FILE
The control file data tracks information regarding the results of using the FIFO Load instruction. This file contains four status bits, the length, and the current position.
0 EN EU DN EM
EM - EMPTY BIT EU - FFU ENABLE
DN - DONE BIT EN - FFL ENABLED

The empty bit is high when the stack is empty. The done bit is set after either a FIFO Load or Unload has been performed. Note that the instruction pairs, FIFO Load and FIFO Unload, use the same control file, since they are accessing the same data...
The FFU and FFL enable bits are set high when those instructions have a false to true logic path transition before them in their respective rung.

The length is the size of the stack. The maximum allowable value is 128. The position is the next available location where words can be entered. This value will be automatically modified by the instruction after it is evaluated...
When you execute this instruction, the new value is placed into the stack and the position counter is incremented so the new value is not overwritten.

This instruction is the FIFO Unload (FFU) instruction, which requires almost all the same parameters as the FFL instruction. The difference is that a destination word location in memory must be specified to store the value being removed from the stack...
CONTROL FILE
0 EN EU DN EM
EM - EMPTY BIT EU - FFU ENABLE
DN - DONE BIT EN - FFL ENABLED
Remember, with FIFO operation, the oldest value on the stack, or first in line, is removed first. This is like having tennis balls in a pipe where you add at one end and remove from the other.
CONTROL FILE
0 EN EU DN EM
EM - EMPTY BIT EU - FFU ENABLE
DN - DONE BIT EN - FFL ENABLED
Remember, the position values of both FFU and FFL are modified by the instructions. Both instructions, if accessing the same stack, use the same control file data and length.
The last instructions we will examine are the LIFO (Last In, First Out) instructions. The principle of operation is the same as the FIFO instruction, just reversed.
2. Use The Programming Device 4. Consult Flow Charts
Imagine that the words are tennis balls entering a tennis ball can.
Once you've placed the balls into the can, you have to remove the last ones you put in before you can get the first ball out..

This means the last ball (word) placed into the can (stack) is the first to be removed. This is how most stacks in microprocessors work. The only disadvantage of this stack is that you have to remove everything above a particular word to get to that word...
This is the LIFO Load (LFL) instruction. This instruction requires the same parameters as the FIFO instruction, but FIFO is replaced with LIFO. Notice the LIFO instruction also uses a control file...
CONTROL FILE
0 EN EU DN EM
EM - EMPTY BIT EU - FFU ENABLE
DN - DONE BIT EN - FFL ENABLED

This is the LIFO Unload (LFU) instruction. Again, this instruction requires the same type of parameters as the FIFO Unload instruction. Remember, however, that the value being removed is the last one that was placed on the stack...
CONTROL FILE
0 EN EU DN EM
EM - EMPTY BIT EU - FFU ENABLE
DN - DONE BIT EN - FFL ENABLED
The FIFO Load and FIFO Unload instructions require two separate control file data elements if they are accessing the same stack.

Remember:::th instructions are using the same stack, they must use the same control file. This file contains the length of the stack and the current position in the stack. If you used two separate control files, neither one would see the changes made by loading or unloading, and the values from the stack would be incorrect..correct...
TRY AGAIN!

If both instructions are using the same stack, they must use the same control file. This file contains the length of the stack and the current position in the stack. If you used two separate control files, neither one would see the changes made by loading or unloading, and the values from the stack would be incorrect...
As you can see, these instructions provide a way for shifting data into and out of locations in memory. In the experiment, you will get to see the operation of the bit shift instruction.

1. The Bit Shift Left instruction is used to shift the bits in a data file in the left direction. The bit shifted out is stored in a status bit of the control file and the bit shifted in is pointed to by the bit address parameter of the instruction.
CONTROL FILE
0 EN DN ER UL NOT USED
1 SIZE OF BIT ARRAYY ER UL NOT USED
2 BIT POINTER
EN - ENABLE DN - DONE
ER - ERASE UL - UNLOAD

2. The Bit Shift Right is used to right-shift the bits in a data file. The bit shifted out is stored in a status bit of the control file and the bit shifted in is pointed to by the bit address parameter of the instruction....
CONTROL FILE
0 EN DN ER UL NOT USED
1 SIZE OF BIT ARRAYY ER UL NOT USED
2 BIT POINTER
EN - ENABLE DN - DONE
ER - ERASE UL - UNLOAD

3. The FIFO instructions, FIFO Load and FIFO Unload, are used to load and unload words from a stack using the First In, First Out method. This method is similar to loading tennis balls into a pipe at one end and taking them out of the other end when necessary.
CONTROL FILE
0 EN EU DN EM

4. The LIFO instructions, LIFO Load and LIFO Unload, are used to load and unload words from a stack using the Last In, First Out method. This method is similar to loading tennis balls into a can and then removing them...
CONTROL FILE
0 EN EU DN EM

Definition
The program shown below is the ladder logic program you will enter to demonstrate the bit shift instructions.
Before entering the program into the PLC APS software, let's look at what the program should do. This will help us understand if the program is operating properly when we test it.
On the 5050-1 PC card there are three switches that we will be using for this program: two push button switches and a slide switch.

The slide switch, which is connected to input I:0/2, is used to set only bit 0 of the output data file to high and the rest to zero. This occurs when the switch is in the right position. We do this whenever we want it initialize the output. to this value..
When the slide switch is in the left position, the contents of the output data file are not modified by the move instruction.

By pressing the START button, we create a false to true logic path for the Bit Shift Right instruction. This instruction has a length of 8, corresponding to the LEDs. Notice that the bit we shift in is the bit we will shift out...

If the STOP button is pressed, we create a false to true logic path for the Bit Shift Left instruction. This now shifts the bits in the other direction. Also, the bit being shifted out (bit 7) is shifted back in.....
When the slide switch is in the left position, the START and STOP buttons shift the output data left right. All values that were shifted out are returned to the other end, making a loop.
The operation of these instructions is very straightforward. We have implemented them into our short program to observe their performance.
